rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites use a verbal clause for their claim to believers but an emphatic nominal clause to assure their own faction of lasting allegiance.
rows.anchor: فقد فَرَّقَ بين قولهم للمؤمنين وقولهم لأصحابهم فقد خاطبوا المؤمنين بالجملة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reason they avoid calling themselves believers is that their beliefs give them no inward motive to say it sincerely.
rows.anchor: إمّا لأن أنفسهم لا تساعدهم عليه إذ ليس لهم من عقائدهم باعثٌ ومُحَرِّكٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the nominal assurance fits their settled Judaism and disbelief, which they gladly affirm and their own group accepts as genuine.
rows.anchor: من الثبات على اليهودية والقرار على اعتقاد الكفر والبعد من أن يزلوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse pairs a purpose verb for night with a nominal predicate for day, combining literal description with figurative attribution for artistic effect.
rows.anchor: فاستعمل مع الليل الفعلَ (لستكنوا فيه) ومع النهار الاسم (مبصراً)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For night, لكم and the purpose verb foreground divine favor; ساكناً would describe a literally quiet night and leave لكم pointless, losing the blessing emphasis.
rows.anchor: فهو جاء بـ (لكم) وبالصيغة الفعلية للدلالة على قصد النعمة والتفضل علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبصراً lets people see in daylight and figuratively makes the day itself see their deeds and witness good and evil, as if it had eyes.
rows.anchor: أنه جعله مبصراً أيضاً يبصر أعمالنا ويكون شاهداً علينا بالخير والشر

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the expressions correspond in meaning; لتبصروا فيه loses the eloquence of figurative attribution, while ساكناً cannot distinguish metaphor from literal description.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت: لِمَ قرن الليل بالمفعول له والنهار بالحال؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet denies idol worship of himself with verbs and nouns, present and past, covering recurring and settled conduct across all times; the unbelievers are denied true worship in nominal form.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أن الرسول نفى عبادة الأصنام عن نفسه بالصيغتين: الفعلية والاسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using only a verb could make the denial seem temporary; using only a noun would mark a trait that might lapse, so both forms affirm the Prophet's complete disavowal.
rows.anchor: إذ لو اقتصر على الفعل لقيل: إن هذا أمر حادث قد يزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the addressees are identified nominally as fixed disbelievers, the denial of their worship of God is also nominal, matching their settled state.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لما اتصفوا بكفرهم على وجه الثبات نفى عنهم عبادة الله على وجه الثبات أيضاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic form follows event character: verbs suit recurring, renewed acts, while nouns suit enduring states and attributes.
rows.anchor: إذا كان مما يتكرر حدوثه ويتجدد استعمله بالصورة الفعلية وإذا لم يكن كذلك استعمله بالصورة الاسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending appears as a present verb in 2:274, 3:134, and 4:38 because it recurs; its sole nominal use in 3:17 describes a stable believer trait.
rows.anchor: الفعل المضارع الدال على التجدد والحدوث لأن الإنفاق أمر يتجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iman often appears as a noun because it is a stable truth residing in the heart, unlike spending, which occurs and stops.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الإيمان له حقيقة ثابتة تقوم بالقلب وليس كالإنفاق يحدث وينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iman takes verbal form when the event is still to occur: the oath concerns future belief upon a sign, and the other verse commands people to believe.
rows.anchor: فجاء به بالصغية الفعلية لأنه هنا أمر دال على الحدوث لا الثبوت فإنه لم يحصل بعد

rows.speaker: البرهان
rows.claim: Al-Burhan distinguishes verbs for renewing realities or effects from nouns for enduring attributes; each form suits its context, including spending versus iman and taqwa.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) "ومن هذا يعرف لم قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istighfar is usually verbal because it recurs, while its sole nominal form in 3:17 describes people as possessing that enduring quality.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك استعماله للاستغفار فإنه لما كان الاستغفار يحدث ويتجدد جاء به بالصيغة الفعلية كثيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih, like istighfar, commonly uses the verb because it is renewed action; 7:206 and 62:1 illustrate this pattern.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك التسبيح فإنه ورد بالصيغة الفعلية كثيراً للسبب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb marks renewal and an active event, while a noun marks settled stability; the Qur'an also uses a participle for a future event treated as already certain.
rows.anchor: فخلاصة الأمر أن الفعل يدل على الحدث والتجدد والاسم يدل على الثبوت والاستقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the appointment has not yet occurred, جاعل presents it as settled and inevitable through the active participle.
rows.anchor: فهو لم يجعله بعد ولكن ذكره بصيغة اسم الفاعل للدلالة على أن الأمر حاصل لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Noah that his people are already certain to drown, using a nominal form instead of the future سيغرقون.
rows.anchor: ولكنه أخرجه مخرج الأمر الثابت أي: كأن الأمر استقر وانتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers to Abraham use a nominal form for the town's destruction to present the announced outcome as fixed, rather than saying سنهلك.
rows.anchor: فذكرها بالصيغة الاسمية للدلالة على الثبات أي: كأن الأمر انتهى وثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:95, the living are paired with a verb for movement and renewal, while the dead are paired with a noun for stillness and stability.
rows.anchor: فاستعمل الفعل مع الحي فقال: (يخرج) واستعمل الاسم مع الميت فقال: (مخرج)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran uses verbs for both life-death transformations because its context depicts change throughout: giving and taking dominion, raising and lowering, day and night, life and death, and provision.
rows.anchor: السياق في آل عمران وهو في التغيير والحدوث والتجدد عموماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Al Imran's change-filled context, Al Anam presents God's attributes, power, and favor; its opening nouns and noun forms fit that setting, with a verb for living movement.
rows.anchor: في حين أن السياق في سورة الأنعام مختلف وليس السياق في التغييرات وإنما هو في صفات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse contrasts an eventful act of calling with nominal silence because speech is a passing response, while silence is the ordinary settled human state.
rows.anchor: الحالة الثابتة للإنسان هي الصمت وإنما يتكلم لسبب يعرض له

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains that people called on God, not idols, in distress; their usual state toward the idols was silence, so either calling or that silence leaves the outcome equal.
rows.anchor: ولِمَ وضعت الجملة الاسمية موضع الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Judgment scene, God describes a completed worldly matter: He did not destroy towns unjustly while their people were unwarned, so the stable nominal form fits.
rows.anchor: فهو في سياق أمرٍ ثبتَ واستقرَّ وانتهى فجاء بالصيغة الاسمية الدالة على الثبوت

words: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ القرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hud's account of worldly life and divine practice, generations change and towns are destroyed over time, so the verb expresses ongoing occurrence.
rows.anchor: فهو - كما ترى - في سياق الدنيا وسنن البقاء فجاء بالصيغة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse uses لم for an event past relative to the Hereafter; Hud uses the lām of denial with a present verb to mark continuity and renewal.
rows.anchor: وجاء ههنا بلام الجحود التي تدخل على الفعل المضارع للدلالة على الاستمرار والتجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's presence averts punishment only for a limited time, so it takes a verb; seeking forgiveness is a lasting deterrent, so it takes a noun.
rows.anchor: فقد جاء في صدر الآية بالفعل: (ليعذبهم) وجاء بعده بالاسم: (مُعَذِّبهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Injustice is a settled cause of a town's destruction; the nominal ظالمون portrays it as a stable quality rather than a passing act.
rows.anchor: فالظلم من الأسباب الثابتة في إهلاك الأمم فجاء بالصيغة الاسمية للدلالة على الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between recurring forgiveness and settled wrongdoing explains why God withholds punishment for repentance yet destroys towns when injustice is entrenched, displaying His mercy.
rows.anchor: فانظر إلى رحمة الله سبحانه وتعالى بخلقه
